text:
lia: FYI Acme POC hitting slow TTFT after we enabled batching + quantized model on dedicated pool. Customer reporting 300-600ms extra on first tokens, some 429s. Can someone jump in?

sam: pinging infra, can you paste the logs or a sample curl? are they on steady small QPS or bursty? :thinking_face:

lia: small sustained QPS (~2 rps) from their e2e test harness. curl looks fine locally. They ran with `batch.max_size=64` and `batch.wait_ms=50`.

maria: that config will prefer batching even at low qps, so it queues a request up to 50ms waiting for a batch — that'll add to TTFT. For small rps we usually recommend `batch.wait_ms=5` or `batch.max_size=8`.

jonah: also seeing some KV cache misses for that customer in the logs. Their prompt prefix changes per user_id which defeats prefix caching.

lia: sample log we got from customer: ```
2026-03-19T14:40:12.312Z inference-gateway INFO request_id=abc123 enqueue_time=50ms batcher=flush_timeout
2026-03-19T14:40:12.362Z runtime WARN model=redwood-3q quantized kv_cache.miss_rate=0.87
2026-03-19T14:40:12.365Z gateway ERROR status=429 reason=rate_limit_shard
```

sam: that 50ms enqueue_time + cache miss is exactly why they're seeing +300-600ms. 429 probably from a shard-level rate limiter kicking in after retries.

maria: quick mitigation steps: 1) drop `batch.wait_ms` to 5ms, 2) `batch.max_size=8`, 3) enable prefix caching (have them normalize prompt prefix), 4) if they need lower latency, try `dedicated.pool_size=1` with smaller concurrency.

lia: customer asked about cost impact of reducing batching (they're worried about tokens cost). any rough numbers?

jonah: batching reduces per-token GPU overhead but increases TTFT at low qps. Rough: moving from 64->8 at this qps will increase compute cost ~5-10% but reduce perceived latency by ~60-80%. Depends on their token length.

sam: also note quantized model reduces VRAM & cost but can increase per-token CPU overhead slightly in our runtime for small batches. If latency is priority, suggest moving to the non-quant model on Dedicated for POC (higher cost but lower TTFT).

lia: customer also sent a security question: will reducing batch size affect isolation / logs? they want assurance.

maria: no change to logging or tenant isolation. batching is per-tenant in Dedicated. We can provide the audit logs for the POC window.

lia: ops-bot: can you pull last 1h of batcher metrics for tenant acme-poc?

ops-bot: metric export queued: https://metrics.internal/redwood/acme-poc?from=1679880000&to=1679883600 (generated by ops-bot) :white_check_mark:

sam: I looked at metrics — avg enqueue_time=37ms, tail 95p=120ms, kv_cache.hit_rate=13%. That confirms both problems.

lia: I'll send recommended config changes and ask them to normalize prefix and re-run. Also will offer to run a short A/B: small-batch non-quant vs big-batch quant.

jonah: if they want immediate stopgap, we can set a per-tenant policy to auto-fallback to small-batch routing when qps<5. I can enable that for acme-poc for the next 24h.

lia: please do that, jonah. I'll update the ticket and include cost note.

maria: quick note for docs: we should add a presales checklist for POC: expected qps, batching defaults, prefix caching guidance, and recommended metrics to monitor (enqueue_time, kv_cache.hit_rate, rate_limit_reasons).

sam: +1, and add a short snippet to the quickstart: `batch.max_size=8
batch.wait_ms=5
prefix_cache.enabled=true`

lia: thanks all — pinging customer to schedule rerun. :thumbsup:

sam: if they still see 429 after these changes, capture `x-retry-count` header and we can trace which shard is rate-limiting.

lia: noted. closing loop after rerun.

jonah: leaving a note: can we also surface a presales toggle in Console to auto-apply low-qps profiles? saves manual work.

maria: agreed, filed feature req in product backlog.

lia: thread ends for now — will post results.
